content.title: What is Transaction Management?
content.description: Transaction Management in JDBC is the process of executing one or more SQL statements as a single logical unit of work. Either all operations succeed (commit) or all operations fail (rollback).

content.content: In database applications, multiple SQL statements often depend on one another. If one statement fails, the database should not be left in an inconsistent state. Transaction Management ensures that a group of operations is treated as a single unit, maintaining data consistency and reliability.

content.title: Why Transaction Management?
content.content: Transaction management maintains data integrity by ensuring that related database operations either complete successfully together or are completely undone.
What is a Transaction?
A transaction is a sequence of one or more SQL operations executed as a single unit. If every operation succeeds, the transaction is committed. If any operation fails, the transaction is rolled back.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: A transaction follows the 'all-or-nothing' principle—either every operation succeeds or none of them are applied.

content.content: Auto-Commit Mode
By default, JDBC operates in auto-commit mode, meaning every SQL statement is automatically committed immediately after execution.

content.title: Disable Auto-Commit
content.code:
Connection con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, password);
con.setAutoCommit(false);

content.title: Important
content.content: To manage transactions manually, auto-commit must be disabled using setAutoCommit(false).
Commit Operation
The commit() method permanently saves all changes made during the current transaction.
Rollback Operation
If an error occurs, the rollback() method reverses all changes made during the current transaction.

Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Bank Money Transfer
content.content: Imagine transferring money from one bank account to another. The amount should only be deducted if it is successfully deposited into the recipient's account. If the deposit fails, the withdrawal should also be cancelled. This is exactly how database transactions work.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Transactions, commit(), rollback(), auto-commit mode, setAutoCommit(false), ACID properties, Savepoint, transaction isolation, and concurrency control are among the most frequently asked JDBC interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why should auto-commit be disabled?
items.answer: Without disabling auto-commit, every SQL statement is committed immediately, making rollback impossible.

items.question: Should commit() be called after rollback()?
items.answer: No. Rollback cancels the transaction, so commit is unnecessary.

items.question: Why must transactions be handled inside try-catch blocks?
items.answer: Exceptions should trigger rollback to maintain database consistency.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: A transaction groups multiple SQL operations into a single unit. Use commit() to save changes and rollback() to undo them when an error occurs.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A transaction is a group of SQL operations.
Disable auto-commit for manual transaction control.
Use commit() to permanently save changes.
